candidates.locator: page 6, section body, table header row (Instream Waste Concentration / criteria columns)
candidates.computation_change_reason: These header formulas define how effluent concentration (Ce) is converted to instream waste concentrations for acute aquatic, domestic-supply chronic, chronic aquatic, and human-health chronic screening; different readings of which formula applies to which use designation would change whether instream concentrations are deemed below chronic criteria and therefore whether effluent limits are established.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, table header row (Need TMDL column)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Need TMDL column signals when a TMDL-based approach may be required instead of a directly calculated numeric limit; interpreting its values (here N/A for all listed pollutants) affects whether an enforceable numeric limit is established versus a non-numeric/TMDL-driven outcome, and whether missing numeric results should be treated as report-only or unresolved.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, table row Diazinon
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row has a blank MQL and multiple 1E+100 criterion entries alongside finite aquatic and human-health values; different interpretations of whether 1E+100 means no applicable criterion, a placeholder, or a binding ceiling would change which Cs is selected, whether the parameter is screened as applicable, and whether monitoring/compliance comparison is required.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, table rows (representative 1E+100 criterion entries)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Repeated 1E+100 values appear across domestic, irrigation, wildlife, acute, chronic, and human-health columns for many pollutants; whether these denote non-applicability, effectively unlimited criteria, or data gaps changes which criterion is treated as most stringent, whether limits are established, and whether absent numeric limits imply no comparison obligation or unresolved evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
STEP 3:            SCAN POTENTIAL INSTREAM WASTE CONCENTRATIONS AGAINST WATER QUALITY CRITERIA
                   AND ESTABLISH EFFLUENT LIMITATIONS FOR ALL APPLICABLE PARAMETERS
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the operative screening step and the scope of parameters subject to limit establishment; interpretation of 'applicable parameters' affects which pollutants receive numeric limits and which monitoring obligations attach to limit-derived compliance.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the receiving stream is not designated for the particular uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Use-designation applicability gates whether any numeric effluent limit is established; different readings of stream use designations would change enforceable limit selection, whether monitoring is for compliance versus informational purposes, and whether missing numeric limits reflect documented non-applicability or unresolved obligation.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the potential instream waste concentrations are less than the chronic water quality criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a screening threshold comparing computed instream waste concentrations to chronic criteria; different interpretations of which chronic criterion applies or how instream concentrations are derived would change whether limits are established and whether associated compliance monitoring is triggered.

candidates.exact_span: The most applicable stringent criteria are used to establish effluent limitations for a given parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Governs selection of Cs among multiple criteria columns in the table; different readings of 'most applicable' or 'stringent' across use classes would change the chosen standard and therefore the calculated daily maximum and monthly average effluent limits.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality criteria apply at the end-of-pipe for acute aquatic life criteria and discharges to public lakes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies an alternate application point for certain criteria, bypassing instream dilution/mixing calculations; whether a discharge or criterion falls within this rule changes whether end-of-pipe values or instream-derived limits govern compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If background concentration exceeds the water quality criteria, water quality criteria apply. And "Need TMDL" shown to the next column of Avg. Mass
candidates.computation_change_reason: Overrides background-driven non-applicability when ambient concentration (Ca) exceeds criteria and links to TMDL need; different interpretations of when background exceeds criteria or how Need TMDL is displayed would change whether numeric limits are imposed and how non-numeric/TMDL outcomes are classified in missing-evidence analysis.

Provides the divisor converting daily maximum effluent concentration to monthly average limit; a different reading of this factor or its interaction with the formula below would change the enforceable monthly average limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS formula block
candidates.exact_span: Daily Max. Conc. = Cs + (Cs - Ca)(F*Qa/Qe)                            Monthly Avg. Conc. = Daily Max. Conc. / 1.5
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is the core limit-calculation formula tying effluent limits to Cs, Ca, mixing fraction F, and flows Qa/Qe; any different interpretation of the formula structure or variable inputs directly changes computed daily maximum and monthly average enforceable limits.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS variable definition Cs
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cs is the criterion value fed into the limit formula; ambiguity in which table column or use-specific criterion constitutes the 'applicable water quality standard' would change all derived effluent limits.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS variable definition Ca
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ca enters the mixing equation and interacts with the background-exceedance rule; different interpretations of which ambient measurement or averaging period defines Ca would change calculated limits.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS variable definition F
candidates.exact_span: F   = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (1.0 is assigned to domestic water supply and human health uses)
candidates.computation_change_reason: F scales allowable mixing in the formula and is fixed at 1.0 for certain use classes; different readings of which use designations trigger F=1.0 versus a lesser fraction would change computed effluent limits.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS variable definition Qa
candidates.exact_span: Qa = Criteria Low flow (4Q3) or Harmonic Mean flow for Human Health Criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Qa selection between 4Q3 low flow and harmonic mean for human-health criteria changes the dilution term (Qa/Qe) and therefore the calculated effluent limit magnitude.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS variable definition Qe
candidates.computation_change_reason: Qe is the effluent flow denominator in the mixing calculation; different interpretations of which flow value, averaging period, or discharge point flow applies would change computed limits.

candidates.locator: page 6, section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS cross-reference
candidates.exact_span: See the current "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico"
candidates.computation_change_reason: Points to external implementation procedures that may govern formula application, F values, flow selection, and parameter applicability; whether and how those procedures are incorporated would change limit calculations and monitoring scope.
